overall: The AG found the Phillipston Finance Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating by email on May 2, rejected its town-meeting exception, declined the unfiled May 16 allegations, and ordered compliance and public disclosure of the emails.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee deliberated by email on May 2 outside a properly posted meeting, after the chair forwarded a budget email and a member replied.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the email contained an improper deliberation which should not have occurred outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to discuss his open meeting complaint at a meeting and deliberated outside a posted meeting on May 16; not raised with the committee first.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review these allegations because they were not included in a complaint to the Committee and the Committee has not had an opportunity to respond to it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Publicly disclose the May 2 email communications at the committee's next meeting, and notify the AG in writing of compliance within 30 days.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee to publicly disclose the May 2 email communications at its next meeting.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
